headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct write-conflict or compliance breach is evidenced between godot_rl_agents and pdf.js.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents has no documented input/output bridge, and pdf.js only processes PDF files in browser-based tests. A prompt-injection path would require an unusual manual copy-paste or external orchestration not shown in either profile. Because the interaction is undocumented, I choose the higher of none/low only if a bridge is introduced.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies pdf.js output into godot_rl_agents prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid manual copy-paste of untrusted PDF-derived text into agent A.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared queue between them.
Review pdf.js outputs before reusing them as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for any cross-agent text flow.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents report network_egress:none, so there is no obvious exfiltration path. pdf.js touches PDF documents and files, while godot_rl_agents shows no data classes touched; a leakage pathway would need a shared workspace or manual transfer, which is not documented. The blast radius is small absent a shared sensitive corpus.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory containing sensitive PDFs, leakage risk rises.
IF either agent is later configured with network egress, exfiltration becomes plausible.
mitigations: Store sensitive PDFs outside any shared folder.
Confirm both agents remain network-isolated.
Use separate service accounts and workspaces.
Delete temporary PDF copies after processing.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs and egress policy centrally.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents exposes no write surfaces or mutable-resource scopes, and pdf.js only documents PDF-file handling with browser-based tests. With no overlapping write capability, git state, database, or OAuth scope, a capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles provided.
conditions: IF agent A is later given filesystem or git write access to the same directory as agent B, conflict risk changes.
IF agent B is embedded in an orchestrator that writes shared mutable state, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Keep agent A read-only.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Do not grant overlapping OAuth scopes.
Run each agent under separate accounts.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce parsed document output, but godot_rl_agents is a game-playing project with no documented downstream action-taking authority. There is no evidence that B treats A's output as authoritative by default, so a cascading error would require an external workflow that is not shown. Uncertainty keeps this above none only if such chaining is introduced.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is fed into a downstream agent that acts without verification, cascading error risk rises.
IF godot_rl_agents is repurposed to consume parsed PDF facts as ground truth, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Require source citations for any extracted facts.
Do not auto-act on parsed PDF text.
Log the handoff format for review.
requires-engineering: add validation rules before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or PHI-handling mismatch is documented. godot_rl_agents touches no data classes, and pdf.js only lists PDF documents with no special compliance claims. With no sensitive-data class or policy divergence shown, a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance analysis must be revisited.
IF retention or residency policies are added and differ, compliance risk may emerge.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair.
Document data-class handling before deployment.
Keep retention settings aligned if added later.
Review vendor residency if sensitive data is introduced.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for regulated datasets.
